artboards.name: cart-page
artboards.role: Cart / checkout review screen for the Forno Rosso pizzeria site. Shows selected order items, delivery destination form, order cost summary, promo code application, and checkout CTA. This is the single artboard in the linked node (the node is a FRAME, not a CANVAS with siblings), so the header, cart-body and footer below are sections of this ONE screen, not separate artboards.

typography.notes: Fraunces (serif, weight 600/700) is used for headings (section titles, brand wordmark, totals label, footer column titles). Geist (sans, weight 400-700) is used for body copy, labels, buttons and nav.

open_questions.topic: Promo code field: only the 'applied' success state is designed
open_questions.detail: This story is specifically about promo code application, but the Figma frame only shows ONE state of the PromoCodeField (13:362-13:370): a code already typed in, validated, with a green border/check icon and a solid-green 'Applied' pill button. There is no drawn default/empty state (with an 'Apply' call-to-action button), no invalid/rejected-code state (e.g. red border + error message), and no loading/submitting state.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Built the default (empty input, neutral border, grey/outline 'Apply' button) and error (red border #C82D25, inline error text, button reverts to 'Apply') states by extension of the existing token palette (--border for default, --brand for error, --success for the drawn applied state), keeping the applied state pixel-faithful to the frame.

options.label: Derive default/error states from existing tokens — neutral #EBE7DF border for empty, brand red #C82D25 for error (assumed)
Request the designer add explicit empty/error/loading frames for this component before building it

open_questions.topic: Two different delivery-time estimates shown on the same screen
open_questions.detail: The header shows 'Estimated delivery: 30 mins' (13:258) while the Delivery Destination card shows 'Est. Delivery: 25-35 mins' (13:328). These could be two different metrics (a global site-wide estimate vs. a destination-specific range) or a design inconsistency.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Treated them as two distinct, intentional data points — a general site ETA in the header vs. a range specific to the entered delivery address — and wired them to separate props rather than reconciling them to one value.

open_questions.topic: No hover/focus state drawn for inactive nav links
open_questions.detail: 'Home' and 'Our Menu' (13:251, 13:253) are only shown in their resting white-text state; only 'Cart' shows the active red-underline treatment. Hover/focus/visited treatments for the inactive links aren't specified.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed a simple color shift to --brand on hover for inactive nav links, matching the active-state color, with no separate focus-ring token defined.

open_questions.topic: Quantity stepper behaviour at minimum quantity
open_questions.detail: Each cart line shows a '-' / count / '+' stepper (e.g. 13:275) but no state shows what '-' does at quantity 1 — decrement to 0 and auto-remove, disable the button, or clamp at 1.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Assumed '-' at quantity 1 removes the line item (equivalent to pressing 'Remove'), since no disabled-button state is drawn.

open_questions.topic: Footer social icons have no link targets in the Figma data
open_questions.detail: Instagram/Facebook/Twitter icon buttons (13:384-13:391) are visual-only nodes; no URLs are attached in the design file.
open_questions.arc_assumption: Left href values as placeholders ('#') pending real social profile URLs from the product/marketing team.
